hints: Look closely at Y and count its carbons to identify exactly which carboxylic acid it is.
Remember that acid hydrolysis of a nitrile gives a carboxylic acid with the same carbon skeleton as the nitrile.
For an ester, focus on the acyl part (the C=O side) because that fragment becomes the carboxylic acid on hydrolysis.
walkthrough:
**Identify compound Y**

First, let's see what we need to make. Y has 3 carbons with a $-COOH$ group.

That is propanoic acid:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Check the nitriles**

Nitriles are hydrolysed by heating with dilute acid to give carboxylic acids with the same number of carbons:
$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, \text{heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
Propanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, so it gives propanoic acid. This works.
Ethanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$, so it gives ethanoic acid with only 2 carbons. This does not work.

**Check the esters**

Esters are hydrolysed by heating with dilute acid to give a carboxylic acid from the acyl part plus an alcohol:
$$\text{R-COO-R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, \text{heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{R'OH}$$
Propyl ethanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so the acid formed is ethanoic acid. This does not work.
Ethyl propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so the acid formed is propanoic acid. This works.

**Combine the conclusions**

Only 1 and 4 give propanoic acid (Y) in one hydrolysis step. That matches the 1 and 4 combination.

options.A: Incorrect. 1 is correct because propanenitrile hydrolyses to propanoic acid, but 3 is wrong because propyl ethanoate hydrolyses to ethanoic acid (from the ethanoate part) and propan-1-ol, not Y.
options.B: Correct. Propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$) gives propanoic acid on acid hydrolysis, and ethyl propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$) gives propanoic acid plus ethanol on acid hydrolysis. Both make Y in one step.
options.C: Incorrect. 2 gives ethanoic acid (2 carbons, one carbon short) and 3 also gives ethanoic acid from its ethanoate portion. Neither gives the 3-carbon propanoic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. 4 is correct because ethyl propanoate gives propanoic acid, but 2 is wrong because ethanenitrile gives only ethanoic acid on hydrolysis.
